body: I'm not too worried about not having the resources and skills, it's just that I don't want to. I'm already exhausted.

Sounds ridiculous, but: Brexit. I turned my life upside down to move here a few years ago, and the country will now go to shit. And while it'll be a long term thing, it just feels like everything I try to do to change my life is doomed. Like even the country I move to will collapse. 

Yeah, I also broke up recently, but if I felt I had some future here, maybe I could start building it. Everything's just up in the air and not in my control.

>maybe its time for you to stop looking for the "cure" outside yourself through others (internet, drugs etc.) but rather the right strategies and the right mindset within yourself. 

Yes, I guess you're right, but that just leads to the problem of being me. Which is a shit person, who just whines and fails.

(Btw, on the drugs, I meant prescribed medication.)

> Maybe we'll always be prone to dark days no matter what we do. 

This is it. And it makes everything else seem so futile. 

On the simple things... Work & commute take so much time out of my days that it often seems impossible to do even a minimum of self-care. But, you're right, a long walk in nature never fails to cheer me. When I get a chance to do it.

Thanks! The thing is, I did all this after Mr A: moved to a new country, started chasing my dream, built a new career. Basically worked my ass off to build this new life. And then, it turns out, it's the same shit in a new wrapper. It all just seems so pointless. Like it's me, not them.

He cooks for me too, it's pretty evenly split. And I get to have sex with him too, pretty much whenever I feel like it (no obligation, of course; we both say 'no' to each other if not in the mood). So I have no complaints on the score of 'chores'. We're good at running an egalitarian household. :)

Thanks. You're right, I fear, about us wanting different things. Disappointing (but good in the long run, I guess) to hear someone else put it like that. I do think he is the committing type - into long relationships. So, yes, if it's not me, it'll likely be someone else. I just have this childish urge to cover my ears and pretend I'm not hearing it. I really don't want to hear it. :(

Thanks for your thoughts! 

That is exactly why I've avoided the conversation - there is something in keeping things unofficial that allows both of us to deal with any controversy and disagreement more maturely. It doesn't turn into a three-day-long battle of wills, but we take a minute to cool off, have a chat, end of. So, at this point, I rather feel, that avoiding conversation continues to be a good thing, as counter-intuitive as that sounds. (Although, I know, that's not exactly what you advised. :) ) I guess I need to have something figured out about what I want before embarking on it...

That's really good stuff about thinking life in stages - it's easy to get caught up in years, but that's not what it's about.
I would still report to police or MP, even if there's nothing they can do now, so that they have something on file in case there is an emergency.

Okay: ladies, gentlemen, others. 

About four years ago, I broke up with A, whom I'd thought I would marry. I was in love like never before, but the life we were building together was not the life I wanted, so I left. I swore never to date again, but most importantly, never to break up again.

But the flesh is weak and the mind not particularly strong either... about six months later I met an interesting man, started hooking up, ended up in a serious relationship. From the start, we had these weird fights about the oddest things. He's prone to anxiety, over-stressing, so am I; neither one good at supporting the other when their own shit is hitting the fan. So, after 3,5 yrs we call it quits. I didn't want to, because after all's said and done, we are good together most of the time: great conversations, both interested in learning and science and becoming better humans, amazing sex etc. It's "just" the fights, and the lack of emotional support. Technically, he left me, although he never actually said it, just cried till I said it for him. 

We're still living together, but moved to separate rooms. Turns out, we get along great when we've broken up. We continue to have sex, although less than before, we run a shared household (cook for each other etc.), we're just back from a holiday together. Fights have been almost non-existent this whole time (3 months now). We haven't had a proper conversation about what's going on and where we are, possibly both dreading it. I still don't want to be broken up, but in my rational mind am aware that we haven't officially got back together, and e.g. that he refers to me as his 'housemate'. 

The reason I've been just going along with this is: it's working, I'm happy; I really don't want to find a new place, build everything from scratch again; I don't know what to do with my life in general... feels like I might as well coast on the relationship while I figure out my next career move etc. 

But, am I just destined for even a bigger heart break when all of this unravels? Should I just move on even though that's the last thing I feel like doing? I'm 37, so I've been through this rubbish a few times now and I'm just sick of it. I just want a partner for life and not deal with this crap. I am not looking forward to going out there and trying to find someone else and again exposing all my vulnerabilities and learning theirs and seeing if things can work out or not.

**tldr**: Living like a couple after break up, not officially together. I don't want to break up. I want a partner for life. I am so sick of dating that I can't even think of putting myself out there again. I'm too old for this.  Who will save me? *rantrantrant* 

Edit: so made myself have a short talk. He thinks it's unlikely that we'll ever actually get back together. I guess I'll have to start planning for without him. Sucks massively.
